note: Description taken from Holmgren's 1910 original description of Eutermes longiarticulatus (in German), including the soldier and worker; alate unknown; type locality Coxipó (Cuyabá), Mato Grosso, Brazil. The author refers Silvestri's E. arenarius subsp. pluriarticulatus var. α to this species. The original is in German and the BHL scan OCR is only moderate: decimal points are often misread as commas or colons and some measurement digits are blurred; blurred values are not cited. The species was then placed in Eutermes and is now in Nasutitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier body length 4.0 mm, head length 1.61—1.79 mm, head width 0.94—1.04 mm (n=3); head capsule smooth, with only a few bristles; frons very weakly arcuately depressed, without an elevation at the base of the nasus; antennae 14-segmented with the segments appearing elongate, from which the species takes its name.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule brown, thoracic and abdominal sclerites rusty brown to rusty yellow. Head smooth, with only a few bristles; abdominal tergites at most microscopically hairy and with distinct marginal bristle rows. Head broadly oval, nasus of normal size; frons very weakly arcuately depressed, without an elevation at the base of the nasus. Antennae 14-segmented: segment 3 only very slightly longer than segment 2, segment 4 only very slightly longer than segment 3, segment 5 shorter than segment 4. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, anterior margin not concave. Measurements: body length 4.0 mm; head length 1.61—1.79 mm; head width 0.94—1.04 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head brown, the head capsule sutures, postclypeus, genae, antennae, mouthparts and the rest of the body white. Cephalic bristles very sparse, abdominal tergite bristles sparse, with marginal bristle rows. Head broadly oval; sagittal suture slightly wider than the transverse suture; frontal marks indistinct; postclypeus slightly shorter than half its width. Antennae 14-segmented: segment 2 almost equal to the sum of segments 3 and 4, segment 3 far shorter than segment 2, segment 4 longer than segment 3, segment 5 indistinctly shorter than segment 4. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped.
